quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Rain pattering on the classroom windows during a lesson"?
quests.hint: Think about when school lessons take place — the sun doesn't need to be visible for it to still be daytime!
quests.explanation: Yes! It's still daytime during school hours, even on a rainy day without visible sunshine.
quests.funFact: Daytime doesn't depend on the sun being visible — it simply means the sun is above the horizon, even behind clouds!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Rain tapping softly on the roof while everyone sleeps"?
quests.hint: Think about when everyone in the house would already be sound asleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Everyone sleeping means it's already night.
quests.funFact: The soft sound of rain can actually help some people fall asleep faster!

quests.instruction: "Kids splashing in puddles wearing their raincoats" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when children are usually outside playing, rain or shine.
quests.explanation: Yes! Playing outside, even in the rain, is usually a daytime activity.
quests.funFact: Rain boots are specially designed to keep feet dry while splashing in puddles!

quests.instruction: "A thunderstorm flashing and rumbling outside a dark window" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'dark' describing the window — what does that tell you?
quests.explanation: Yes! A dark window during a storm tells you it's already nighttime.
quests.funFact: Lightning can actually make the night sky brighter for just a split second!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Gray clouds covering the sky while children walk to school". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when children usually walk to school, even under a cloudy sky.
quests.explanation: Yes! Children walk to school during the day, even if clouds are covering the sun.
quests.funFact: Even on the cloudiest day, the sun is still shining above the clouds!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Fog rolling silently over a moonlit field". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'moonlit' — when does moonlight shine?
quests.explanation: Yes! Moonlight only shines at night, so this foggy field is seen after dark.
quests.funFact: Fog can make moonlight look even softer and more mysterious as it drifts through the air!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Wind blowing leaves across the playground during recess"?
quests.hint: Think about when recess happens during the school day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Recess is a playtime break that happens during the school day.
quests.funFact: Windy days can make leaves swirl and dance in fun, unpredictable patterns!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Wind rattling the windows as the household settles in to sleep"?
quests.hint: Think about when a household would be settling in to sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! A household settling in to sleep tells you it's already nighttime.
quests.funFact: Strong winds can happen at any time, but they often sound extra noticeable in a quiet, sleepy house!

quests.instruction: "A foggy morning as the school bus drives carefully down the road" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'morning' — which part of the day does it belong to?
quests.explanation: Yes! Morning is part of the daytime, even when fog makes it harder to see.
quests.funFact: Bus drivers use extra caution and slower speeds on foggy mornings to stay safe!

quests.instruction: "Snow falling silently and piling up under the streetlights" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when streetlights are actually switched on and glowing.
quests.explanation: Yes! Streetlights are on at night, lighting up the falling snow beneath them.
quests.funFact: Snow can actually make nighttime streets look brighter, since snow reflects light so well!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Snow falling gently while children build a snowman". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when children are usually outside playing in the snow.
quests.explanation: Yes! Building a snowman is an outdoor activity usually enjoyed during the day.
quests.funFact: No two snowflakes have ever been found to look exactly the same!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Storm clouds blocking the moon so completely that the sky looks pitch black". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about whether you truly need to see the moon for it to still be nighttime.
quests.explanation: Yes! It's still nighttime even when clouds hide the moon completely — the moon is still up there, just hidden.
quests.funFact: On very cloudy nights, the sky can look pitch black even with a full moon hidden behind the clouds!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Thunder rumbling in the distance during an afternoon storm"?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'afternoon' — which part of the day is that?
quests.explanation: Yes! Afternoon is part of the daytime, even during a stormy moment.
quests.funFact: You can estimate how far away a storm is by counting the seconds between lightning and thunder!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A misty, cool breeze drifting through an open window at bedtime"?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'bedtime' — it's a strong clue all by itself.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bedtime happens at night, right before sleep.
quests.funFact: A cool breeze at bedtime can actually help some people fall asleep more comfortably!

quests.instruction: "A cloudy sky with no sunshine, yet the park is still full of families" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about whether you truly need to see the sun for it to still be daytime.
quests.explanation: Yes! It's still daytime even without visible sunshine — clouds just hide the sun, they don't erase the day.
quests.funFact: The sun is always up there during the day, even when thick clouds completely block our view of it!

quests.instruction: "Thick clouds hiding the stars, yet the whole town is still fast asleep" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about whether you truly need to see the stars for it to still be nighttime.
quests.explanation: Yes! It's still nighttime even without visible stars — clouds just hide them, they don't erase the night.
quests.funFact: The stars are always up there at night, even when thick clouds completely block our view of them!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The very first activity each morning: waking up and stretching". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about what happens right as someone opens their eyes in the morning.
quests.explanation: Yes! Waking up and stretching happens first thing in the morning, starting the day.
quests.funFact: Stretching after waking up can help wake up your muscles and get your blood flowing!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The very last activity before falling asleep: closing your eyes". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about what happens right as someone drifts off to sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Closing your eyes to fall asleep happens at night, ending the day.
quests.funFact: It usually takes most people between ten and twenty minutes to fully fall asleep!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Right after breakfast, brushing teeth for the very first time that morning"?
quests.hint: Think about when breakfast happens, and what usually follows it.
quests.explanation: Yes! Brushing teeth after breakfast happens in the morning, during the day.
quests.funFact: Dentists recommend brushing your teeth at least twice every day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Right after dinner, getting the bath ready before bed"?
quests.hint: Think about when dinner usually happens, and what comes after it.
quests.explanation: Yes! A bath after dinner, before bed, happens in the evening or night.
quests.funFact: A warm bath before bed can actually help your body relax and feel ready for sleep!

quests.instruction: "The midpoint of school hours, between morning and afternoon classes" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what sits between morning and afternoon — both are part of the same time of day.
quests.explanation: Yes! The middle of a school day is still part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Many schools schedule lunch right around this midpoint of the day!

quests.instruction: "The midpoint of a long sleep, hours after everyone said goodnight" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what sits in the very middle of a long night's sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! The middle of a long sleep is still deep in the nighttime.
quests.funFact: Our bodies do a lot of important resting and growing during the middle of a good night's sleep!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "The moment the final school bell rings to end classes". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when school usually lets out — is the sun typically still up?
quests.explanation: Yes! School usually ends in the afternoon, while it's still daytime.
quests.funFact: The very first school bells were rung by hand, long before electric bells existed!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "The moment the house finally falls completely silent". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when a busy house would finally become completely silent.
quests.explanation: Yes! A house usually falls completely silent once everyone is asleep, at night.
quests.funFact: A quiet, calm environment can help everyone in the house sleep more soundly!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Coming home from school and starting on homework"?
quests.hint: Think about when children usually get home from school to begin homework.
quests.explanation: Yes! Coming home from school and starting homework usually happens in the afternoon.
quests.funFact: Taking short breaks while doing homework can actually help you focus better!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Finishing a bedtime story and settling in under the covers"?
quests.hint: Think about when a story like this is read, right before sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bedtime stories are finished right before sleep, at night.
quests.funFact: Reading together before bed is a favorite tradition in families all around the world!

quests.instruction: "The sun beginning to dip lower after a long afternoon of play" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about whether the sun has fully set yet, or if it's just getting lower.
quests.explanation: Yes! A dipping sun that hasn't set yet still means it's daytime.
quests.funFact: The sun appears to move slower when it's high in the sky and faster near the horizon!

quests.instruction: "The sky finishing its slow fade from evening light to full darkness" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what the sky looks like once this slow fade is finished.
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the sky finishes fading to full darkness, night has arrived.
quests.funFact: This slow fading time, between sunset and full darkness, is called twilight!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A snack break between finishing homework and starting dinner". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when homework and dinner usually happen — is the sun typically still up?
quests.explanation: Yes! This snack break happens in the late afternoon, while it's still daytime.
quests.funFact: A healthy snack can help keep your energy up between activities!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A late snack of warm milk right before turning off the lights"?
quests.hint: Think about what happens right after this warm, late snack.
quests.explanation: Yes! A late snack right before turning off the lights happens at night, just before sleep.
quests.funFact: Warm milk before bed is a cozy tradition that many families enjoy!
